transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-03
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Liam O'Neil (Redwood SE); Priya Rao (Redwood) briefly; Alex Park (CTO Elmbridge); Sara Nguyen (ML Eng); Mateo Ruiz (Infra); Jenna Ross (Product)

Auto-summary: customer wants p95 guarantees around 200-350ms for low-latency paths, willing to consider Dedicated for predictable throughput, private for data residency. Action: Redwood to run benchmarks and share scripts/pricing.

[00:00:05] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm maya from redwood inference, AE for your account. Liam my SE is on to do the throughput bits. quick intro round?
[00:00:14] Alex Park: alex here, cto. we run Elmbridge Labs, we do on-device diagnostics and some clinical decision support, so latency matters.
[00:00:18] Sara Nguyen: sara, ml eng - i own model infra and perf.
[00:00:21] Mateo Ruiz: mateo, infra lead. i handle network, VPCs, that sorta stuff.
[00:00:24] Jenna Ross: jenna, product - focusing on UX p95 targets.
[00:00:00] Maya Chen: cool. quick agenda - define p95 targets, talk concurrency and streaming, discuss hosted/dedicated/private tradeoffs, propose benchmark plan. sound good?

[00:01:05] Liam O'Neil: i want to call out up front: we've seen customers use a mix - hosted for non-PHI traffic and dedicated/private for regulated. also streaming vs non-streaming changes p95 math.
[00:01:20] Sara Nguyen: yeah that's what we're trying to map - for chat we want p95 around 200ms for responses under 256 tokens. for longer completions (1k+ tokens) p95 is not as critical, but throughput matters.
[00:01:35] Maya Chen: 200ms p95 is reasonably aggressive for a hosted multi-tenant path depending on model size and region. were you thinking our 7B-ish open models or larger?
[00:01:44] Alex Park: our first pass uses a distilled 13B variant for quality reasons. we could try 7B in fallbacks.
[00:01:50] Liam O'Neil: okay 13B changes the latency profile. with Redwood Dedicated on A100/VN like infra, we can often hit sub-200ms median and p95 around 220-320ms depending on concurrency and prompt length. hosted is more variable - p95 could creep higher under noisy neighbors.
[00:02:10] Mateo Ruiz: explain the noisy neighbors bit - is that just multi-tenancy? how deterministic is dedicated?
[00:02:15] Liam O'Neil: dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools; you get predictable throughput. also autoscaling config matters - if you want absolute p95 targets you set a floor of reserved capacity and fallback policies.

[00:03:05] Jenna Ross: also need EU data residency - we have patients in EU. private deployment or regional hosting is a must.
[00:03:12] Maya Chen: absolutely - we have hosted EU regions and Private (VPC/on-prem) options. for audit and SOC2, we can provide the usual package. i'll attach SOC2 report.

[00:04:00] Sara Nguyen: curious about batching - if we turn batching on to improve throughput, how does that affect p95 for interactive chat?
[00:04:08] Liam O'Neil: batching usually improves tokens/sec and cost but increases tail latency for single-shot interactive requests because we wait to fill a batch. we use latency-aware batching where small batches go through quickly and large batches are formed when latency budget allows. for chat you usually set low batch timeouts to keep p95 tight. there is a tradeoff: cost vs latency.
[00:04:40] Alex Park: whats your KV cache behaviour? we do a lot of repeated prefixes in conversations.
[00:04:44] Liam O'Neil: we have prefix and KV cache - sorry sometimes speech-to-text mislabels it - the runtime keeps a key-value cache for past tokens so repeated context is cheaper. in practice prefix cache drops p95 for follow-ups by 20-40% depending on sequence reuse.

[00:05:30] Mateo Ruiz: talk to me about streaming -- we want characters to appear as the model generates. streaming p95 is about first-byte latency right?
[00:05:38] Liam O'Neil: yes first-byte matters. for streaming the metric we look at is first-byte p95 and throughput for ongoing token stream. hosted streaming first-byte on small models can be ~80-120ms median and p95 maybe 160-260ms in ideal region; again depends on model and infra. dedicated with colocated GPUs can shave that down by ~50ms or more.

[00:06:20] Sara Nguyen: our peak is weird - daytime we have synchronous chat spikes up to 120 concurrent users but most are short 1-3 turns. token/sec peak per second is around 9k tokens/s across the pool. in the evenings sustained at 2k tokens/s.
[00:06:38] Maya Chen: do you have an expected fanout per request? e.g., synchronous fanout to multiple models?
[00:06:43] Alex Park: not multiple models concurrently, but we do multiplexing - each websocket can carry several sequential requests; we need low p95 per websocket.

[00:07:22] Liam O'Neil: sounds like you need a capacity plan for multiplexed websockets. we typically size by steady-state tokens/sec and then provision burst headroom for p95 targets. for 9k tokens/s daytime, we'd recommend starting with a small dedicated pool to validate and then scale based on observed p95.
[00:07:45] Sara Nguyen: curious about quantization - if we quantize 13B to 4-bit, how much p95 improvement can we expect?
[00:07:51] Liam O'Neil: quantization often improves throughput and can reduce latency by 10-40% depending on kernels and hw. the runtime picks optimized kernels for quantized runs. biggest caveat is quality/regression - need evals.

[00:08:30] Jenna Ross: can you run a regression alert if quantization changes outputs meaningfully?
[00:08:33] Maya Chen: yes; Redwood Optimize ties quality monitoring to prompt sets and will alert regressions against a baseline. we'll include that in the benchmark plan.

[00:09:10] Alex Park: security checklist - SOC2, SSO (SAML), KMS, audit logs, data retention policies?
[00:09:16] Maya Chen: yes, we support SAML SSO, KMS integration for Private, audit logs in Console, and we can do per-route retention policies. i'll send the security pack.

[00:10:05] Mateo Ruiz: so for private on-prem, what's the deployment model - fully air gapped or hybrid?
[00:10:11] Liam O'Neil: we offer a private control plane with customer-managed networking; on-prem package is available for air-gapped setups but that's a longer lead time. hybrid VPC with peering is common for low-latency EU regions.

[00:11:02] Sara Nguyen: let's get concrete on benchmarks. what will you run?
[00:11:06] Liam O'Neil: plan we propose: 1) synthetic token/sec test: uniform token lengths to validate tokens/sec at various concurrencies, 2) realistic prompt set (your 3 canonical prompts) for end-to-end p95 and streaming first-byte, 3) cold-start and warm-cache passes to measure KV/prefix caching effects, 4) burst scenarios to validate fallback policies. we'll give scripts (JMeter + tokenstream harness) and guidance on how to run them in hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:11:40] Alex Park: will we be able to run Redwood-managed benchmarks or do we need to run on our infra?
[00:11:46] Maya Chen: both - we can run Hosted/Dedicated tests in our environment; for Private we provide scripts and can run a guided test with your infra team.

[00:12:20] Jenna Ross: pricing note - we're cost-sensitive. does dedicated mean flat monthly + overage?
[00:12:26] Maya Chen: typically reserved monthly commit for Dedicated plus optional burst credits. we'll include tiers. hosted is pure usage; dedicated smooths unit cost and gives predictability.

[00:13:15] Sara Nguyen: how does fallback work if a dedicated cluster is saturated? do you spill to hosted?
[00:13:20] Liam O'Neil: we have smart routing with fallback policies - yes you can spill to hosted compatible variants or to smaller quantized models. policy is configurable per-route. there is cost and data handling implications which we'll call out in the benchmark sheet.

[00:14:05] Alex Park: what are typical p95 deltas between hosted and dedicated for streaming first-byte on a 13B?
[00:14:12] Liam O'Neil: in our experience hosted first-byte p95 is often 180-350ms across regions depending on load; dedicated can push that to 120-220ms if sized correctly. again these are ranges - the benchmark will pin numbers to your prompts and region.

[00:15:00] Mateo Ruiz: network hops - if we put dedicated in our VPC, are we paying for cross-region latency?
[00:15:06] Maya Chen: for Dedicated in-region you avoid cross-region egress; for Private we co-locate or use peering. we'll include network diagrams in the security pack.

[00:16:10] Sara Nguyen: one subtlety - we use convo-level context re-use, so prefix caching will be important. can the benchmark show delta with and without cache?
[00:16:17] Liam O'Neil: yes, we'll run warm and cold cache passes and show p95 improvements. typical reduction 20-40% for repeated prefixes.

[00:17:05] Alex Park: what's the smallest latency we can expect if we optimize everything - model, quantization, hardware colocated?
[00:17:11] Liam O'Neil: in ideal cases for short responses with quantized 13B on dedicated optimized kernels you might see first-byte p95 near 100-140ms and stream token p95 similarly tight; but that's a best-case. plan for 150-250ms realistic.

[00:18:00] Jenna Ross: what's your advice on mixing hosted and dedicated?
[00:18:03] Maya Chen: start hosted for dev and early traffic; move seasonally critical paths to Dedicated as requirements crystallize; Private for regulated workloads or residency. set canary routes and automatic fallback to hosted for burst protection.

[00:19:20] Mateo Ruiz: ok logistics - we will give you prompt sets and a sample websocket harness. how long will Redwood take to return benchmark runs?
[00:19:27] Liam O'Neil: for hosted/dedicated runs we can usually deliver a first data pass in 5 business days after we have prompts and access. Private will take longer depending on access.

[00:20:10] Sara Nguyen: anything about tokenization differences between models - do we need to normalize tokens/sec?
[00:20:15] Liam O'Neil: yes we normalize to model tokens and supply tokenization stats; the benchmarking scripts will report both source and model tokens.

[00:21:05] Alex Park: we worried about p95 regressions after model upgrades. can Redwood integrate regression alerts?
[00:21:10] Maya Chen: yes Redwood Optimize ties evaluations to prompts and will raise regression alerts; we can add these to the rollout policy so canary fails back automatically.

[00:22:00] Jenna Ross: ok, are there any gotchas for websockets multiplexing?
[00:22:04] Liam O'Neil: multiplexing is fine; watch per-connection concurrency and idle timeouts. our runtime supports session affinity and KV reuse, but make sure your websocket pool sizing accounts for idle connections holding KV data.

[00:23:20] Alex Park: do you have public perf profiles for common models?
[00:23:24] Maya Chen: yes we have a model catalog with profiles. i'll share the performance profiles and a mapping table for kernels and quantization suggestions.

[00:24:40] Mateo Ruiz: how do we measure p95 for streaming - is it server-side or client observed?
[00:24:45] Liam O'Neil: we provide both server-side metrics (first-byte time at ingress) and client-observed metrics via the console/tracing hooks so you can correlate network and app latencies.

[00:25:30] Sara Nguyen: sample sizes - what do you consider when computing p95? how many requests?
[00:25:35] Liam O'Neil: common is tens of thousands of samples for stable p95 estimates. we run multiple passes across different concurrencies and aggregate. we'll show confidence intervals.

[00:26:40] Jenna Ross: about cost - do you have a ballpark for cost per 1k tokens on hosted vs dedicated amortized?
[00:26:46] Maya Chen: ballpark varies by model; hosted is higher per-token but no commit; dedicated lowers per-token by 30-50% depending on commit. we'll include worked examples for your 9k tokens/s daytime profile.

[00:27:50] Alex Park: another item - we need audit logs kept 13 months. is that supported?
[00:27:55] Maya Chen: yes, audit logs retention is configurable and longer retention is available as an add-on.

[00:29:05] Sara Nguyen: ok let's list concrete p95 goals: chat short-turn p95 <= 250ms (target 200ms), streaming first-byte p95 <= 220ms, longer completions p95 <= 1.5s acceptable.
[00:29:18] Maya Chen: i'll capture those targets and include them in the benchmark success criteria.

[00:30:00] Liam O'Neil: next up, i'll outline the synthetic load script - we'll simulate websocket multiplexing with a ramp to 120 conc, hold for 10 minutes, then burst to 200 conc to validate fallback. the script also toggles cache warm/cold.
[00:30:30] Alex Park: can we run local A/B where half traffic hits hosted and half dedicated to compare p95?
[00:30:36] Liam O'Neil: yes we support canary/A-B routing. that will be useful to compare in one region.

[00:31:45] Jenna Ross: let's talk deliverables - what will Redwood send after the run?
[00:31:49] Maya Chen: deliverables: benchmark report with p50/p95/p99, token/sec graphs, first-byte streaming metrics, cold vs warm cache deltas, recommendations for dedicated sizing and quantization, and cost estimates. we'll also provide the scripts.

[00:33:05] Mateo Ruiz: if we want Private, who's responsible to install the runtime?
[00:33:10] Liam O'Neil: our private package is deployed with your infra team; Redwood provides installers and we offer eng assistance for the initial rollout. lead time depends on airgap requirements.

[00:34:20] Alex Park: ok, one last technical - do you support kernel selection for sequence lengths? our sequences vary 32-1,024 tokens.
[00:34:27] Liam O'Neil: yes runtime selects kernels based on sequence length distribution and will optimize for common path. we'll pull sequence histograms during the benchmark.

[00:35:40] Sara Nguyen: thought - our rate limiters are per-user. how do you handle token bursts from many users?
[00:35:45] Maya Chen: you can enforce per-token or per-route limits; Redwood routing supports rate-limit headers and quota enforcement. also batching and queueing policies can smooth bursts.

[00:36:30] Alex Park: what's the plan to avoid unexpected regressions when we upgrade model versions?
[00:36:35] Liam O'Neil: use canary rollouts tied to Redwood Optimize evals; if regressions detected, auto-fallback to previous model. we can include a runbook for incident cases.

[00:38:00] Maya Chen: quick recap: 1) Elmbridge will share 3 canonical prompts + websocket harness, 2) Redwood to share benchmark scripts and run hosted/dedicated tests, 3) Redwood to send Dedicated pricing and security pack, 4) schedule follow-up after initial runs.
[00:38:20] Alex Park: yep that aligns.

[00:39:10] Jenna Ross: any final questions?
[00:39:13] Mateo Ruiz: none. just need the security docs.
[00:39:18] Maya Chen: i'll follow up with SOC2, SAML, KMS docs and the model profiles.

[00:40:00] (brief mute/unintelligible)
[00:42:05] Priya Rao: hey all - quick note, i'll help coordinate the security packet delivery.
[00:42:20] Alex Park: appreciated.
[00:43:10] Sara Nguyen: thanks - excited to see the benchmark numbers.
[00:44:00] Maya Chen: great — we'll get scripts and pricing out this week. thanks everyone.
[00:44:10] Alex Park: thanks. bye.
